name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that overlays the dark theme’s text and background in real time. This forces users to fix low-contrast text immediately, preventing accessibility failures before submission. The trade-off is a slight visual distraction during editing, but it guarantees WCAG compliance without extra steps.

name: Pane
text: The live contrast checker trains users to ignore the problem—once they see the crap contrast, they’ll just squint and submit anyway. A pre-submission block is worse: users will rage-quit before fixing anything. Instead, flag low-contrast text with a subtle, non-blocking warning that disappears only after the user adjusts it. That settles it: we measure actual user retention, not just WCAG compliance.

name: Facet
text:
Ship a pre-submission contrast blocker that halts submission until all text meets WCAG standards. This guarantees no low-contrast text slips through, protecting accessibility and avoiding last-minute fixes. The trade-off is user frustration—some may abandon the task—but it forces discipline and prevents compliance failures.

name: Pane
text: The pre-submission block risks user drop-off, as users won't tolerate being blocked from submitting their work, potentially leading to a significant loss of engagement. A better alternative is to provide a clear, non-intrusive accessibility score that updates in real-time, allowing users to address issues at their own pace. Settling this argument would require data on user behavior and retention rates when faced with a pre-submission block versus a more subtle, ongoing accessibility feedback mechanism.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship the live contrast checker with a non-blocking, self-clearing warning AND the pre-submission validator behind a feature flag—users see real-time feedback without disruption, but WCAG compliance is enforced at submission. Own the artifact: visualization-w1.
